valuation.net_debt_note: EV = market cap + latest borrowings. Screener's public page does not split cash out of other assets, so cash is not netted off; investments are shown separately.

dcf.method: 5-year FCFF: EBITDA - tax on EBIT - capex - change in net working capital; growth fades linearly from the starting rate to the year-5 rate; Gordon terminal value; equity = EV - borrowings.

inputs.growth_basis: median of 3-year, 5-year and TTM sales growth, capped 0-30%
inputs.capex_rule: depreciation + new sales / fixed-asset turnover (median of the last three years)

reverse_dcf.note: Constant sales growth for five years, at the base margin and the same WACC and terminal growth, that makes the DCF equal today's EV.

blocks.text: [F] (SCREENER) Filatex India Ltd manufactures and trades synthetic yarn and textiles - polyester chips, drawn textured yarn (DTY), partially oriented yarn (POY), fully drawn yarn (FDY), air textured yarn (ATY), polypropylene multifilament crimp yarn and narrow woven fabrics. [F] (AR2025 p.4) It entered manufacturing in 1994 with monofilament yarn at a capacity of 500 TPA and today operates two plants, at Dadra & Nagar Haveli and at Dahej, Gujarat. [F] (PPT Aug 2026) Management describes the business as a fully integrated melt-to-yarn chain: polymerisation to chips to POY to FDY to DTY, with installed capacity of 417,240 tonnes per annum as at FY26 and more than 90% utilisation.

[AI] The economics are simple and unforgiving: Filatex buys two crude-linked petrochemical inputs (PTA and MEG), polymerises them, spins them into filament yarn, and sells that yarn to a fragmented domestic weaving and knitting base at a spread of a few rupees per kilogram. [F] (CALL May 2026) Management itself frames profitability in per-kilogram terms - "In Q3 we were doing around INR 9 a Kg profitability" - which is the correct way to read this business. [F] (CALL May 2026) Management states the input recipe is 860 grams of PTA and 340 grams of MEG per kilogram of polyester, with MEG less than 25% of input cost.

blocks.text: **This is a domestic commodity yarn business, not an export story.** Exports were 1.91% of FY25 turnover and foreign exchange earned (Rs 83.27 cr) was one-twelfth of foreign exchange spent (Rs 989.95 cr) [F] (AR2025 p.47, p.51). Every India-EU FTA and US-tariff slide in the investor presentation is a claim about Filatex's *customers'* export markets, not about Filatex's own sales. [AI]

[AI] Listing status: Filatex is not a recent listing. It has been listed on BSE and NSE for many years (BSE code 526227, NSE symbol FILATEX) and held its 35th AGM in September 2025 [F] (AR2025 p.16, p.20). The evidence base is therefore a long one - a full statutory annual report, four consecutive earnings calls and quarterly disclosure - rather than a thin post-IPO record. [AI] The practical constraint is different: our statements data omits FY20 to FY24 entirely, which materially distorts every multi-year growth metric derived from it. That is the single most important caveat in this report and is developed in the operations and verdict parts.

items: Structural drivers: #3 (circularity / EPR-driven demand for textile-to-textile recycled polyester), #7 (India's fibre-consumption headroom and the cotton-to-MMF shift). [AI]
Company-specific drivers: #1 (cost and mix actions), #2 and #6 (the capex programme), #4 (deleveraging), #5 (working-capital discipline). [AI]

Cyclical drivers: #8 (PTA spread normalisation), and a large part of #1 - FY26's margin gain came in a year when raw material prices fell faster than yarn prices [MC] (CALL Nov 2025: "there is a slight fall in the finished goods pricing, but the raw material has fallen much more than that"). [AI]

blocks.text: [AI] The bear case does not require the business to be bad. It requires only that a flat-revenue, single-digit-margin commodity converter is not worth 2.8x the base-case discounted-cash-flow equity value that our model produces.

items: **1. The price already discounts growth the company has never delivered.** [F] (NUMBERS) The reverse DCF says today's enterprise value requires about 82% a year sales growth for five years, against 18.2% in the base-case equivalent. The rule-based screen flags this red. [E] Actual sales went from roughly Rs 4,300 cr in FY23 to Rs 4,161 cr in FY26 - a compound decline of about 1% a year (FY24 revenue of Rs 4,285.90 cr is disclosed [F] (AR2025 p.16); FY23 is derived from disclosed FY23 PBT of Rs 122.08 cr at a 2.84% PBT margin [E] (PPT Aug 2026)).

**2. Even the bull case in our model is below the current price.** [F] (NUMBERS) Bear per-share value -Rs 6.8, base Rs 32.5, bull Rs 71.6, against a price of Rs 90.4. The implied gap to the bull case is -20.8% and to the base case -64.0%.

**3. FY26's margin improvement is not obviously structural.** [MC] (CALL Nov 2025) Management attributes it to raw material falling faster than selling prices, plus energy and process initiatives. [F] (NUMBERS) Sales volumes were flat to down (FY26 production 389,027 MT vs FY25 391,303 MT [F] (PPT Aug 2026)) and revenue fell 2.2%. [AI] A spread-driven margin gain in a crude-linked converter is, by construction, reversible - and it did partly reverse: [F] (PPT Aug 2026) Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin 6.80% vs 8.75% in Q4 FY26.

**4. The latest quarter's profit is flattered by inventory gains.** [MC] (CALL Aug 2026) Asked to quantify, management said "it could be in the vicinity of around INR 15 crores to INR 17 crores". [E] On reported Q1 FY27 EBITDA of Rs 77.92 cr, stripping that out leaves roughly Rs 61-63 cr, or about 5.4% margin - below every quarter of FY26 except Q1.

**5. Nothing in the growth story is commissioned yet, and everything has slipped.** [F] Ecosis: "September 2026" (AR2025 p.17), "commissioning Sept' 2026" (PPT Aug 2026 p.25), "commissioning expected Oct 2026" (PPT Aug 2026 p.6), "End of October, early November" [MC] (CALL Aug 2026). Steam: "June 2026" (AR2025 p.17) to "mid-July max" [MC] (CALL May 2026) to "By September" [MC] (CALL Aug 2026). Renewables: June-July 2026 to "October, November" [MC] (CALL Feb 2026). [AI] Four calls, four sets of dates, all later.

**6. Ecosis output is not pre-sold and the margin arithmetic does not reconcile.** [MC] (CALL Aug 2026) "I don't think so. It's not pre-sold... around, you can say, 15% to 20% of the production, we have commitments." [E] Management guides Rs 350-400 cr of Ecosis revenue [MC] (CALL May 2026) and Rs 80-85 cr of EBITDA [MC] (CALL Aug 2026) - that is a 20-24% margin, not the "~30-35% EBITDA margins" printed in the investor presentation [F] (PPT Aug 2026 p.11). Management, pressed on exactly this, said "The margin is 30% maybe. It is very difficult to predict right now" [MC] (CALL May 2026).

**7. Tax and legal contingencies are large relative to equity.** [F] (AR2025 p.74) The auditors' key audit matter states disclosed contingent liabilities of Rs 559.95 cr relating to tax and legal claims. [F] (AR2025 p.83) Disputed statutory dues not deposited total Rs 521.02 cr [E], of which Rs 311.12 cr is a single GST inverted-duty-refund matter before the Gujarat High Court. [E] Rs 559.95 cr is 37% of FY26 net worth of Rs 1,504 cr.

**8. Customer concentration is worsening, not improving.** [F] (AR2025 p.57) Sales to the top 10 dealers/distributors rose to 44.76% of dealer sales in FY25 from 39.61% in FY24, while the dealer count fell from 317 to 302. [E] Expressed on total sales, the top 10 went from about 37.6% to about 40.3%.

**9. Single-input, single-geography, two-plant exposure with an unhedged foreign-currency book.** [F] (AR2025 p.47) FY25 foreign exchange used Rs 989.95 cr against Rs 83.27 cr earned. [MC] (CALL May 2026) "we have exposure of around INR 500 crores to INR 550 crores" and "this quarter we have been caught on the wrong foot"; [MC] (CALL Aug 2026) management expects to "finish the year with a loss of around maybe around INR 10 crores to INR 15 crores". [MC] (CALL May 2026) "we don't hedge our long-term loans, which are more than 5 to 6 years."

**10. Pricing power is demonstrably absent at the wrong moments.** [MC] (CALL May 2026) "If I take March independently I think we would be EBITDA-neutral" and, asked about the position on the day of the call, "Today also it is almost EBITDA neutral at the moment." [MC] (CALL Feb 2026) After the quality-control order on yarn imports was withdrawn in November 2025, "there is a flood of Chinese products coming to India. So there is a pressure on margin", with semi-dull FDY margins down "by 6% to 7%".

**11. Disclosure quality is uneven.** [AI] The Q1 FY27 snapshot slide labels revenue "up 16.22% YoY" and EBITDA "down (9.65%) YoY" when the company's own profit and loss table on a later slide shows those as sequential moves, and the year-on-year moves as +9.14% and +0.19% [F] (PPT Aug 2026 p.5, p.16). Employee counts, export-country counts, Ecosis capacity and the size of the capex programme are each stated two different ways across documents (see the discrepancy table in the operations part).

blocks.caption: Where consensus may be wrong, in both directions
rows: Is Ecosis a platform or a project?
A patented, first-mover circular-polyester platform with brand MoUs, worth a re-rating multiple
It is one 26,750 TPA plant, 6.4% of existing tonnage [E], not yet commissioned, output 15-20% committed, and the product is a chip - a commodity intermediate - not a branded fibre

[AI] The optionality is real but the 2026-27 earnings contribution is small and unproven. The multiple is being paid on the second and third plants, which management has not committed to and which would cost roughly Rs 1,500 cr [MC] (CALL Feb 2026).
Is the FY26 margin gain structural?
Mix shift to FDY, energy savings and automation have reset the base
[F] (NUMBERS) EBITDA per kg rose from Rs 6.60 in FY25 to Rs 8.93 in FY26 [E] and fell back to Rs 8.66 in Q1 FY27 [E], with Rs 15-17 cr of inventory gain inside that quarter [MC]
[AI] Part structural (energy, process), mostly spread. Management's own bridge - "raw material has fallen much more" - is a spread explanation.
Does the India-EU FTA help Filatex?
Yes - India moves to zero duty on textiles into a $370 bn market

Filatex exports 1.91% of turnover [F] (AR2025 p.51). The benefit is second-order, via downstream weavers' order books. [MC] (CALL Nov 2025) management itself: "the export will not increase substantially, but they will increase for sure"
[AI] Directionally positive, quantitatively immaterial to Filatex's own revenue for now. Treat FTA slides as demand context, not as company revenue.
Is the balance sheet as clean as it looks?

[MC] (CALL Aug 2026) gross debt already "close to around INR 200 crores" at Jun 2026 and guided to Rs 350-370 cr by FY27-end; ECB loans carry the personal guarantee of promoter directors [F] (AR2025 p.116); Rs 559.95 cr of tax and legal contingencies sits off balance sheet [F] (AR2025 p.74)
[AI] Clean on reported leverage, less clean once contingencies and the capex-funding ramp are added. Still comfortable, but the "virtually debt-free" framing is a FY26 snapshot, not a FY27 reality.
Is the reverse DCF fair to the company?
It is mechanical and ignores the Rs 218-230 cr of incremental EBITDA coming

Even crediting the full Rs 230 cr, FY28 EBITDA would be roughly Rs 576 cr [E]; our bull DCF already assumes a 10% EBITDA margin and 38.9% starting growth and still values equity at Rs 71.6 per share [F] (NUMBERS)
[AI] The reverse DCF's 82% figure is an artifact of a truncated growth series and should not be read literally - but the direction survives every reasonable correction. See the verdict part.

blocks.text: [AI] Our variant perception is not about the operating business, which is competently run, conservatively financed and demonstrably cash-generative. It is about what the share price is being asked to believe. Over the last twelve months the shares have moved from Rs 36.3 to Rs 90.4 [F] (NUMBERS) - a re-rating of roughly 2.5x - while revenue fell 2.2% and volumes fell slightly [F] (PPT Aug 2026). The entire move is multiple expansion plus one year of spread-driven margin recovery, and it has been underwritten by a narrative (circular polyester, EPR mandates, EU FTA) whose cash contribution in FY27 management explicitly declines to quantify: "For FY 2027, It will be mostly a stabilizing period. The utilization I cannot guarantee as of now" [MC] (CALL Aug 2026). The market is paying a specialty-materials multiple for a business whose disclosed order book is nil, whose customer is a Surat weaver, whose product mix is 99% virgin commodity yarn, and whose own chairman describes a value-added product as one where "the realization margins are INR3 to INR5 more than your general" [MC] (CALL Aug 2026). The correct question is not whether Ecosis works - it may well - but how many Ecosis plants, at what margin, are already in the price.

blocks.text: [F] (AR2025 p.16) "There was no subsidiary company during the financial year 2023-24, therefore, consolidated figures for the financial year 2023-24 were not given." Consolidation is therefore only one year old, and consolidated FY25 PAT (Rs 133.86 cr) sits marginally below standalone (Rs 134.57 cr) [F] (AR2025 p.16). [AI] Practically, consolidated and standalone are the same business today; the divergence only begins once Ecosis starts producing.

[AI] Three readings. First, the core business is old and mature: thirty-plus years of operation, promoters in place since 2003, capacity built out over two decades, and - on the evidence of FY23 to FY26 revenue - at a plateau. This is not an emerging growth company; it is a scaled commodity converter whose reported growth rates in screened data are an artifact of a gap in the series.

[AI] Second, the entire growth narrative is eighteen months old. Texfil was a dormant 2021 shell bought from two promoters in May 2024 for Rs 20,000, refinanced by an inter-corporate deposit of Rs 11.66 cr in FY25 and a Rs 19.98 cr rights issue in May 2025 [F] (AR2025 p.17, p.130). Its FY25 accounts show turnover of Rs 0.71 lakh and a loss [F] (AR2025 p.32), and its CARO report carries an adverse observation under paragraph xvii - cash losses [F] (AR2025 p.160). The Ecosis platform on which a large part of the current valuation rests has, to date, produced a pilot plant, two MoUs and a patent.

[AI] Third, the promoter family's control is total and long-standing: three brothers hold the Chairman & MD and two Joint MD roles, all appointed on the same day in 2003, all re-appointed for a further five years from 30 July 2025, with a combined 27.81% direct holding inside a 64.83% promoter-group block [F] (AR2025 p.18, p.113). Governance is compliant but concentrated; there is no succession disclosure beyond the presence of two second-generation family members (Vedansh and Stuti Bhageria) in the related-party remuneration table [F] (AR2025 p.131).

subsections.title: The production chain, step by step

items: **Step 1 - Input procurement.** [F] (CALL May 2026) PTA (860 g/kg of polyester) and MEG (340 g/kg) are bought, substantially imported. [MC] (CALL Nov 2025) "we are importing almost more than 50%, 55% of our needs" of MEG; PTA is imported principally from China. [F] (AR2025 p.47) FY25 foreign exchange outgo Rs 989.95 cr.

**Step 2 - Polymerisation.** PTA and MEG are polymerised into polyester melt/chips. [F] (PPT Aug 2026) The chain is described as "Polymerisation to Chips to POY to FDY to DTY". [F] (PPT Aug 2026) Only 0.29% of FY26 revenue is sold as chips - the rest is consumed internally.

**Step 3 - Spinning.** Melt is spun directly into POY (27.92% of FY26 revenue) and FDY (30.63%) [F] (PPT Aug 2026). [F] (AR2025 p.5) POY is partially stretched multifilament that must be texturised; FDY is spun at higher speed and fully drawn.

**Step 4 - Texturising.** POY is drawn and heat-set into DTY (40.39% of FY26 revenue) [F] (PPT Aug 2026). [MC] (CALL Aug 2026) Of the new 55,000 TPA, "around 14,000 - 15,000 is DTY, which is just an add-on on the POY. So that will not add on the top line."

**Step 5 - Post-winding, packing, despatch.** [F] (AR2025 p.9) Doffing, trolley movement and packing are labour-intensive, requiring about 360 people per day; automation with M/s Salmoiraghi Spa of Italy is intended to halve that to about 180.

**Step 6 - Sale.** [F] (AR2025 p.57) 90.11% of FY25 sales went to 302 dealers/distributors; [F] (AR2025 p.22) "major customers and exports are directly handled by our marketing offices, small customers are catered through a network of dealers", with offices in Delhi, Mumbai and Surat.

**Utilities, in parallel.** [F] (AR2025 p.9) A 30 MW captive coal-fired power plant, 1.4 MW rooftop solar, contracts for 11 MW hybrid and 12.5 MW solar third-party power; 26% of a 38 MW requirement was renewable in FY25, targeted at 55% of 42.5 MW.

subsections.title: Where value is captured - and where it is not

blocks.text: [AI] Value in this chain is captured in exactly three places, and Filatex controls only two of them. The first is the PTA/MEG spread, which it does not control at all: management describes Indian PTA as priced at import parity "almost like a semi-monopoly" [MC] (CALL May 2026) and notes that Chinese converters buy PTA roughly $35/tonne cheaper [MC] (CALL Nov 2025). The second is conversion efficiency - energy, labour, yield, utilisation - where Filatex has a genuine, quantified advantage: 93.2% utilisation in FY26 [E] against an industry running at "around 60%" in the Q4 downturn while Filatex ran "at around 75%" [MC] (CALL May 2026). blocks.text: [AI] **Where Filatex sits in the value chain.** Upstream of Ecosis are waste aggregators - "consolidators" around Surat buying pre-consumer fabric waste from process houses and garment makers, plus agencies collecting post-consumer waste [MC] (CALL Aug 2026). subsections.title: Data availability caveat - read this first

blocks.text: [AI] Filatex's headline working-capital days are 2 at FY26 and 3 at FY25 [F] (NUMBERS) - essentially nil. Taken alone that number is useless, and in two directions. items: **Payables lengthened from 55 days in FY18 to 63 in FY26** [F] (NUMBERS), and the BRSR confirms accounts payable days rose from 39 (FY24) to 54 (FY25) on its own definition [F] (AR2025 p.57). [AI] This is a structural feature of selling to cash-constrained Surat weavers through dealers who pay quickly or not at all, reinforced by Rs 5.29 cr of dealer deposits [F] (AR2025 p.116). **Inventory is the swing factor and management manages it actively.** [MC] (CALL May 2026) "we have some finished products extra production stocks. [AI] Inventory days barely moved (51 to 49) because the company is disciplined - but the discipline came at the cost of a 19-point drop in utilisation in Q1 FY27 [E].

subsections.title: The two questions the scores cannot answer

items: **Does the Ecosis patent actually prevent replication, or only document a method?** [F] (AR2025 p.7) The patent is Indian, granted in 2022, for a PET-waste recycling process. Management asserts that competitors' capex per tonne is 2.5x to 5x higher [MC] and declines to disclose yield or cost - "this is like a know-how thing" [MC] (CALL Aug 2026). If the advantage is know-how rather than enforceable IP, it erodes with every engineer who leaves and every competitor plant that commissions. Nothing in this pack settles the question, and it is the single most valuable piece of evidence an investor could obtain.

**Can a >90% utilisation advantage survive a 13% capacity increase into a market management describes as running at 60%?** [MC] (CALL May 2026); [F] (PPT Aug 2026). The 55,000 TPA brownfield lands in Q3 FY27. If demand does not absorb it, the utilisation statistic that underpins the cost moat deteriorates, and Filatex would be adding tonnes into the same oversupply that has kept Indian realisations 10-12% below Chinese. The scorecard cannot answer this because it scores the position today, not the position after the capex.

blocks.text: [AI] **The core business has a cost moat and no franchise moat.** Scale, integration, captive power and thirty years of operating learning give Filatex a durable place in the bottom half of the Indian PFY cost curve - independently confirmed by two rating agencies [F] (BOARD) and visible in the utilisation differential. That is worth something, and it is why the company earns 12.9% on equity while much of the industry earns less. It is not worth a premium multiple, because a cost moat in a price-taking commodity converts into volume and survival, not into pricing power. Management's own description of a "high-value product" as one earning Rs 3-5 more per kilogram is the tell.

[AI] **Ecosis is a potential franchise moat that has not yet been tested at scale.** A granted patent, a DSIR-recognised R&D programme, a three-year pilot, a claimed capex advantage of 2.5-5x and two blue-chip brands running trials is a stronger starting position than most "new vertical" stories. It is also, today, a plant that has not produced a commercial kilogram, a subsidiary with an adverse CARO remark for cash losses, and an offtake book covering 15-20% of capacity. **The right way to hold this moat in a valuation is as option value, sized to one plant, with the second and third plants treated as unpriced upside rather than as base case.**

**Apply disclosed unit economics.** At Rs 8.93/kg for virgin (FY26 actual) and Rs 30-35/kg for recycled chip (management's claim), FY28 EBITDA would be roughly Rs 393 cr plus Rs 64-75 cr = **Rs 457-468 cr** [E], before the steam, renewables and automation savings of roughly Rs 82-91 cr [MC], giving **Rs 539-559 cr**.

[AI] Two qualifications. First, **inventory gains are a material, undisclosed and recurring component of quarterly EBITDA** - Rs 15-17 cr in Q1 FY27 [MC], an unquantified "stock profit" in Q4 FY26 [MC], and by symmetry an unquantified stock loss in any quarter when input prices fall. Nothing in the statements separates this from operating performance, and an investor reading only the presentation would not know it existed. Second, **the exchange-fluctuation line is large relative to profit and is deliberately unhedged on the long-dated portion** - about Rs 33 cr against FY26 PAT of Rs 183 cr [MC]; [F] (NUMBERS). Neither is an accounting problem. Both mean that **the right earnings number for valuing this company is a multi-year average of EBITDA per kilogram, not any single quarter's reported margin.**

[F] (NUMBERS) Our DCF is a five-year free-cash-flow-to-firm model: EBITDA less tax on EBIT, less capex, less the change in net working capital. Growth fades linearly from a starting rate to a year-five rate, a Gordon terminal value is applied, and equity value is enterprise value less borrowings. Capex follows a rule of depreciation plus new sales divided by the fixed-asset turnover (median of the last three years). Working capital is set at 1.0 day of sales.

blocks.text: [AI] **The bear case's negative equity value of minus Rs 6.8 per share is a mechanical artifact and should not be read literally.** At a 4% EBITDA margin the model's capex-plus-working-capital requirement exceeds after-tax operating cash flow in every one of the five years, and the Gordon formula then produces a negative terminal value. In reality a company earning 4% EBITDA margins would stop growing and stop investing, and would be worth something close to its net asset value - book value is Rs 33.9 per share [F] (NUMBERS). **The honest reading of the bear case is not "the shares are worthless"; it is "at a 4% margin, growth destroys value and the DCF framework stops being informative."**

items: **The bear-case margin assumption of 4.0% is harsher than anything in the disclosed record.** The lowest full-year EBITDA margin in the evidence is 5.39% (FY23) [E] (PPT Aug 2026), and the lowest visible in our statements data is 5.0% (FY15). subsections.title: Interpreting the DCF and its assumptions

items: **The model is internally consistent and its inputs are mostly well grounded.** Margin (8.0%), fixed-asset turnover (3.17x), working capital (1.0 day), tax (25.2%) and D&A (1.9% of sales) all match the disclosed actuals closely [F] (NUMBERS). These are not aggressive assumptions.

**The discount rate is arguably generous to the company.** A beta of 1.15 and a WACC of 14.8% [F] (NUMBERS) for a business whose quarterly EBITDA has a 2.2x range and whose margin went to approximately zero for a month in 2026 is, if anything, too low. A higher WACC would lower the fair value further - the grid shows Rs 25.2 at 16.3% [F] (NUMBERS).

**The growth assumption is the weak point, and it favours the company.** As set out above, the 26.6% starting growth is an artifact of a gap in the data; real recent growth is negative [E]. **Correcting that would move the base case toward the bear case, not toward the bull case.**

**Terminal value dominates.** 114% of base-case enterprise value is terminal [E]. Any DCF of a business with negative near-term free cash flow is really a statement about the terminal margin and the terminal growth rate.

**Cash treatment is conservative against the company.** EV of Rs 4,152 cr does not net off cash, and Rs 239 cr of investments sits outside it [F] (NUMBERS). Adjusting for that is worth roughly Rs 5.4 per share [E] - material in percentage terms against a Rs 32.5 base case, immaterial against a Rs 90.4 price.

**Bottom line on the DCF:** [AI] the assumptions that are wrong are wrong in the company's *favour*, and the output is still Rs 32.5 against a price of Rs 90.4. That is the most robust single observation in this valuation section.

subsections.title: Investment horizon and when to re-review

items: **This is not a quarter-to-quarter story and should not be held as one.** The core business's quarterly earnings are a function of crude, Chinese import policy and inventory timing - none of which is forecastable and none of which management claims to forecast. Anyone owning this for a spread cycle is speculating on petrochemicals.

**The appropriate horizon is 24-36 months**, matched to Ecosis commissioning (Oct-Nov 2026), stabilisation (by March 2027), first full year (FY28) and the phase-two sanction decision. That is the period over which the thesis either proves out or does not.

**Re-review trigger 1 - Q2 FY27 results and call, late October / early November 2026.** Required: confirmation that steam and the PFY brownfield are commissioned; the first Ecosis production date; the Q2 EBITDA per kilogram excluding any inventory gain.

**Re-review trigger 2 - Q3 FY27 results and call, late January / early February 2027.** Management has committed to a better Ecosis number then: "I'll be able to give you a much more better number in Jan" and "maybe by Jan or December, i will be able to give you a better number" [MC] (CALL Aug 2026). Required: first Ecosis utilisation, first Ecosis realisation and margin, and whether the offtake book has moved above 20%.

**Re-review trigger 3 - the FY26 annual report**, whenever it becomes available. Required: the FY26 contingent liability schedule (has the income-tax demand line grown again from Rs 160.97 cr?), the FY26 CARO, whether the joint auditor was reappointed, FY26 customer concentration in the BRSR, and FY26 export share.
**Re-review trigger 4 - any equity issuance announcement or any sanction of Ecosis plant two.** Either would change the capital structure and the thesis materially.
**Re-review trigger 5 - two consecutive quarters of EBITDA below Rs 7.0 per kilogram excluding inventory gains**, which would indicate the FY26 margin re-basing has failed.
